newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses hit records, gold and oil dip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses hit records, gold and oil dip.

text.p: The London stock market hit record highs on Thursday after fears eased of higher interest rates and Frankfurt also scaled new peaks as European bourses recovered from Wednesday's late profit-taking.
Wall Street weighed in with solid gains in early trading.
Recovering from a shaky opening, the London market, Europe's busiest, climbed on news of slower inflation and confirmation that British interest rates would stay at six percent for now.

By mid-afternoon it had stalled just short of the 4,200 level on the key FTSE 100 share index. "The market's just incredible," said one trader. "Obviously the inflation data helped and the pressure on interest rates has been relieved."
The Paris bourse also neared a new trading peak during a session in which key French interest rates, like those in London, were left at current levels.

Gold, weakened recently by competition from a firmer dollar and booming stock markets plus concern over central bank gold sales, edged lower. Oil also declined after a weather-related leap upwards on Wednesday.
On the currency markets, the dollar was fairly steady after what market analysts said was an expected correction following a move above 1.60 marks and a 46-month high against the yen.

"We're seeing a correction after the dollar's rise to 1.60 marks but we don't see that progressing too much further. Similarly, the downside looks fairly limited on the yen," said Ian Gunner, senior economist at Chase Investment Bank.
On balance, economists had not expected a British interest rate rise yet despite the Bank of England's known desire for higher rates to contain inflationary risks.
But surprisingly strong British jobless data on Wednesday, with unemployment falling to a six-year low, had raised a few doubts and jangled market nerves.

The London stock market opened a little easier on Thursday. But it was then reassured by news that inflation slowed to 2.5 percent last month from November's 2.7 percent and the decision to keep interest rates unchanged.

Wall Street stocks, meanwhile, revived from a bout of profit-taking on the previous day and headed higher, boosted by firmer bonds and favourable earnings reports. The Dow Jones industrial average was up around 36 points after an hour, having ended 35.41 lower at 6,726.88 on Wednesday.

French stocks gained ahead of a Bank of France meeting at which dealers and economists said its intervention rate could be trimmed to 3.10 percent from 3.15 -- but wasn't. They stayed firm afterwards but slipped a little from their highs.
The French central bank's monetary council meeting, which left rates unchanged, was the first since the appointment of two new members seen to lean more towards faster rate cuts.
Frankfurt, meanwhile, joined London in rewriting the record books, closing floor trade at a record for the DAX index, just short of the 3,000 level. Dealers said the rally was not over.
"The champagne bottles will be out," said one trader. "There is more in this market. The uptrend is definitely still there."
Gold, however, slipped from the previous London close to below $354 amid concern that other central banks might follow the Dutch and sell more of their gold reserves, traders said.
"In the coming months and years, European central banks will gradually reduce their gold reserves," one Zurich trader said.
World oil prices, which had recovered in late trade on Wednesday amid concern over cold U.S. weather, also eased.
London February futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend were down 19 cents at $23.65 a barrel.

Elsewhere, the Bank of Spain made a cut of a quarter point to six percent in its key money rate, surprising markets despite the peseta's strength and benign inflation. The peseta responded by strengthening to 83.43 to the mark from 83.70 overnight.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT

The dollar was quoted around 116.75 yen and 1.5940 marks, compared with 117.17 and 1.5912 late on Wednesday. Sterling, after weakening following the interest rate news, revived to around 2.6735 marks from 2.6701 overnight.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of top British shares was up 35.6 at 4,194.5, after hitting an all-time high of 4,198.9.

Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 4.86 at a new closing high of 2,993.31 after an all-time record of 2,998.61 earlier. The IBIS DAX for electronic trade was up 17.10 at 2,993.66 after a record 2,998.79 earlier.
In Paris, the CAC-40 index was up 20.34 at 2,408.32 versus Wednesday's intra-day record of 2,418.93.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold slipped to an afternoon fix of $353.05 from a morning setting of $354 and previous close of $354.15. Silver added around two cents to $4.72.
